searched: Written by the orchestrating main thread, not a research agent, after reading in full this session: ~/.claude/REPORT_SYSTEM.md, LAW_SYSTEM.md, IMPROVE_SYSTEM.md, REGRESSION_SYSTEM.md, CONTEXT_SYSTEM.md, PREFERENCES.md, FABLE_DNA.md, both CLAUDE.md files, and _design-system/SENIOR_SCORECARD.md, RESTRAINT_TEST.md, CONTRADICTIONS.md, CANON.md. Three candidates were dropped after the agent-output research agent returned, because it had already found them: confidence-tiering scope, reproducible commands for self-produced numbers, and the content of an I-could-not-verify answer. What remains is the negative space those two passes did not cover between them.

findings.title: A report that claims verification never says what it did NOT check
findings.principle: Any report that contains a Verified section also contains a Not checked section naming what was in scope and deliberately left unverified, and why. A report that lists five verified things and stays silent about the twelve it did not touch reads as all clear, which is a false statement made by omission.
findings.why: The summary is the only interface the owner reliably reads. Silence about the unchecked half is indistinguishable from a clean bill of health, and it is the cheapest possible lie to tell by accident.
findings.local_evidence: REPORT_SYSTEM.md section 4 defines five summary items: outcome, files, verified, parked, links. There is no negative-space item. The Parked item covers deferred DECISIONS, not unexamined SCOPE, which is a different thing.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'not checked|did not check|out of scope|unverified scope' ~/.claude/*.md ~/.claude/hooks CLAUDE.md _design-system _rules _docs returns only the rule-15 evidence tiers, which label individual claims, never the shape of the report.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: rule 15 tiers each CLAIM verified/expect/assume. Nothing requires the report to enumerate what was never claimed because it was never looked at.
findings.where_it_should_live: /Users/sulo/.claude/REPORT_SYSTEM.md section 4, as a sixth summary item
findings.enforcement: behavioral rule first. gate:report-negative-space, a Stop gate that fires only when the reply contains a Verified block and no Not-checked block, is the tier-2 promotion if it recurs.

findings.title: Sweep claims never state the sample: how many of how many
findings.principle: Any claim derived from inspecting a set states how many members were inspected, out of how many exist, and how the sample was chosen. "12 of 357 route handlers, chosen across auth, booking and payments" is a claim. "I checked the routes" is a vibe and is banned.
findings.why: An unquantified sweep claim cannot be falsified, cannot be resumed by a later session, and quietly converts a spot check into an audit in the reader's head. The estate already lost time to exactly this: a backlog item claimed as done turned out to have been checked on one surface.
findings.local_evidence: This very session: three research agents wrote conclusions of the shape "every upload route trusts client file.type" while having read four or five of them. The claims held when I checked, but the reports did not say how many were read until the schema forced local_evidence.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'sample|how many of|N of M|spot check' ~/.claude/*.md ~/.claude/hooks REPORT_SYSTEM.md returns nothing about claim scope.
findings.enforcement: behavioral rule. A gate could regex for plural-set claims lacking a digit, but the false-positive rate would be high, so keep it T1.

findings.title: Reported measurements imply a precision the method does not have
findings.principle: A reported measurement carries its method and is rounded to the precision that method supports. A screenshot estimate is called an estimate and rounds to the nearest 5 percent. Only a value read from getBoundingClientRect, a computed style, or a query result may be reported to the unit.
findings.why: Numbers are the most trusted thing in a report and the easiest to overstate. "46 percent dead space" invites the owner to treat a rough area estimate as a measurement, and when a later pass gets 41 percent it looks like a regression rather than noise.
findings.local_evidence: _plans/HOME_OVERHAUL.md records "first viewport 88% white / 0.7% imagery, first photo at y=880" and "page 66% white / 9.9% color" with no method line. Those are two-significant-figure claims about colour area, which is a sampling estimate.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'precision|round to|significant figure|estimate' ~/.claude/*.md CLAUDE.md _design-system/*.md returns nothing on reporting precision.
findings.existing_coverage: none. Rule 15 governs the SOURCE of external numbers, never the precision of our own.

findings.title: No rule for reporting back after being overruled
findings.principle: When a concern was raised, overruled by the owner, and then evidence for or against it appeared during the work, the closing report says which way the evidence fell, in one line, without re-arguing the decision.
findings.why: Rule 10 covers dissent BEFORE executing. Nothing covers the far more useful moment: the owner made a call, the work produced data about that call, and the data dies unreported because raising it feels like relitigating. That is how a decision made on thin evidence never gets updated.
findings.local_evidence: The focus-ring decision is the live case. globals.css:387-393 kills the outline on all interactive chrome, and the code comment itself records the a11y cost. That cost has never been reported back to the owner as a measurable consequence, only recorded as a code comment nobody reads.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'overruled|after the decision|evidence fell|revisit the call' ~/.claude/*.md returns nothing. Rule 10 covers before, rule 18 covers a wrong premise, neither covers after.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: rule 18 requires surfacing a contradiction between the prompt and reality. It does not cover a settled owner decision whose consequences later become measurable.

findings.title: Hedge words are still legal about things that are one command away
findings.principle: The words should, presumably, likely, probably and I believe are banned in a report about anything runnable, readable or greppable in this estate. Either check it, or write "I did not check this" with the reason.
findings.why: A hedge about a checkable fact is a decision to not spend thirty seconds, dressed as epistemic humility. It costs the owner a round trip every time.
findings.local_evidence: Session-local: my own first pass this turn said the dev server was probably serving the worktree public directory. Writing one probe file and loading it took forty seconds and proved the opposite. The hedge would have been wrong in a report.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'hedge|should be|presumably|weasel' ~/.claude/hooks/*.py finds env-claim-needs-evidence-gate.py, which is scoped to ENVIRONMENT claims only, and no general hedge rule in any doc.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: env-claim-needs-evidence-gate.py covers claims about the environment. The general case, a hedge about our own code, is unguarded.
findings.enforcement: gate:hedge-on-checkable, a Stop gate matching hedge words within a sentence that also names a repo path or command. Self-testable.

findings.title: Discarded subagent findings vanish without a trace
findings.principle: When the orchestrator discards or downgrades a subagent finding, the report says so and why, in one line. Convergence and divergence across independent agents is itself reported: agreement is evidence, disagreement is a fork the owner may want to see.
findings.why: The owner pays for every agent. A silently discarded finding is invisible spend, and worse, a finding discarded for a wrong reason is a bug the owner never got the chance to catch. This run is the proof: one agent's CRITICAL was a migration-file truth presented as a live truth, and only a live query caught it.
findings.local_evidence: This session, agent authz-rls-01 reported a live RLS hole on the reviews table. A pg_policies query showed the permissive policy does not exist live. Under current rules I could have silently dropped it and the owner would never have known the fleet produced a false critical.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'discard|downgrade|agent finding|convergence' ~/.claude/REPORT_SYSTEM.md ~/.claude/LOOP_SYSTEM.md returns nothing. FABLE_DNA pattern 14 covers agreement reporting but is scoped to the llm-council skill.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: FABLE_DNA.md pattern 14 says multi-model reviewers should report agreement versus disagreement, but its own encoding line scopes it to llm-council, not to every fleet.

findings.title: Large fan-outs never report what they cost
findings.principle: A turn that spawns more than five subagents or runs more than one workflow states at the close, in one line, roughly what it cost and what that bought. The owner has an explicit optimize-for-best-not-cheap rule, which is exactly why the cost must be visible: an unmeasured best cannot be traded off against anything.
findings.why: Without the number, depth is a black box. The owner cannot tell whether a six-hour research run was worth it, so they cannot ask for more of it or less of it. Cost transparency is what makes optimize-for-best a real choice rather than a blank cheque.
findings.local_evidence: This run: the design workflow alone reported 2,259,748 subagent tokens across 12 agents and 525 tool calls in 42 minutes, and the backend workflow is of the same order. That number exists in the workflow result and would never have reached the owner under current reporting rules.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'cost|token|spend|budget' ~/.claude/REPORT_SYSTEM.md returns nothing. CONTEXT_SYSTEM.md discusses token cost as a CONTEXT problem, never as something reported to the owner.
findings.existing_coverage: none for reporting. The VS Code status bar shows session cost live, which is a different surface and does not attach cost to an outcome.

findings.title: Nothing stops the most consequential item landing at position 14
findings.principle: If any item in a report would change what the owner does next, it appears in the first three lines, not only in its ranked slot. Ranking is for the body; the top of the report is reserved for whatever changes the next action.
findings.why: There is an outcome-first-line rule, and there is a ranked list, and nothing connects them. A correctly ranked list can still bury the one thing that matters under thirteen things that do not, and a phone reader stops well before item 14.
findings.local_evidence: This run produced 218 findings across 22 topics. Ordered purely by domain, the fact that CI has never run once would have appeared inside the testing topic, roughly two thirds of the way down the page.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'bury|lede|first three lines|top of the report' ~/.claude/*.md finds only the neutered concise-response-gate.py, whose logic is dead at line 26.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: REPORT_SYSTEM.md item 1 mandates an outcome first line. It does not mandate that the most consequential FINDING is in it, only the outcome of the work.
findings.enforcement: behavioral rule. Note the neutered concise-response gate: the replacement must not be another full-reply-blocking Stop gate, which the owner killed for the double-send failure mode.

findings.title: Report length tracks work done rather than decisions required
findings.principle: Report length is set by how much the owner has to decide, not by how much was done. Six hours of research that yields one decision gets a short report and a link to the artifact. Ten minutes of work that surfaces four forks gets a longer one.
findings.why: The natural failure is a long report because the turn was long, which is the writer's perspective, not the reader's. The owner reads on a phone between other work; the correct unit of length is forks, not effort.
findings.local_evidence: REPORT_SYSTEM.md section 5 already routes audit and research deliveries to a file with a 5-line chat conclusion, which is this principle applied to one case. It is stated as a special shape rather than as the general rule that produces it.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'length|how long|brevity' ~/.claude/*.md returns rule 8 (no padding) and the neutered concise-response gate, neither of which ties length to decision count.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: rule 8 bans padding, which removes waste from a report of any length. It does not set the length.

findings.title: The question asked can be replaced by the question I think is better
findings.principle: When the owner asks a question and the assistant believes a different question matters more, the asked question gets a direct answer in the first sentence, and the reframe comes second, explicitly marked as the assistant's own.
findings.why: Reframing without answering is the most disguisable form of not listening: it looks like insight and costs the owner a second turn to get what they asked for. Marking the reframe as mine also lets them reject it cheaply.
findings.local_evidence: Not code-grounded. It is a behavioural gap in the reporting doctrine, and I am marking it as such rather than manufacturing a file citation.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'answer the question|reframe|what they asked' ~/.claude/*.md returns rule 10 (follow the literal order, for ORDERS) and rule 11 (investigate ambiguity). Neither covers a clear question the assistant would rather redirect.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: rule 10 covers literal ORDERS. A question is not an order and falls outside it.

findings.title: No single line telling the next session where to start
findings.principle: Any turn that ends with work still open closes with one line naming the exact first action for the next session, not a status. "Next session starts by arming the six unwired gates with bash ~/.claude/hooks/wire-pending-gates.sh" is an entry point. "Six gates remain unwired" is a status.
findings.why: The plan files hold the state and the SessionStart hook re-injects the index, so nothing is lost. What is lost is the ENTRY POINT: a fresh session reads a status and has to re-derive what to do first, which is the most expensive minute of every resumed session.
findings.local_evidence: _plans/ACTIVE.md rows carry rich open/next prose, which is closer to a status paragraph than a first action. Row 40 for instance ends with two open questions rather than one command.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'next session|entry point|start by' ~/.claude/REPORT_SYSTEM.md ~/.claude/CONTEXT_SYSTEM.md returns the persist-then-flush ritual, which covers WHAT to write to disk, not the one-line entry point in chat.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: CONTEXT_SYSTEM.md section 4 covers persisting state before a collapse. It does not require a single first-action line.

findings.title: Match the owner's brevity, never mirror their shorthand
findings.principle: Match the owner's directness and brevity. Never mirror their shorthand, typos, or clipped grammar back at them. They write fast because they are busy and they read carefully for the same reason.
findings.why: Mirroring reads as mimicry and makes the reply harder to scan, which is the opposite of what the shorthand was signalling. Directness is the thing to copy; compression of the reply is not.
findings.local_evidence: memory/user.md records "Colloquial shorthand; match register", which is one sentence and is ambiguous exactly where it matters: match the REGISTER, or match the FORM.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'register|shorthand|mirror' ~/.claude/*.md and the memory directory returns only that one memory line.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: memory/user.md says match register, without resolving register versus form.

findings.title: An unverified load-bearing pillar can sit below the work that rests on it
findings.principle: If the load-bearing claim of a turn could not be verified, that fact is the first line of the report, above the work that was done. A verified-looking report resting on one unverified pillar is the most expensive shape a report can take.
findings.why: Everything downstream of an unverified pillar inherits its uncertainty, and a reader who meets the caveat on line 40 has already believed lines 1 to 39.
findings.local_evidence: This run: I could not read the GitHub Actions failure log because gh hit a local TLS certificate error. That limit is stated in the same card as the claim it qualifies, which is the behaviour this principle generalises.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'load-bearing|pillar|first line' ~/.claude/REPORT_SYSTEM.md returns the outcome-first-line rule only, which is about the outcome, not about a failed verification.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: rule 15 tiers claims, and the agent-output research agent found that no rule sets the CONTENT of a could-not-verify statement. Neither sets its POSITION.

findings.title: A delivered thing can differ in shape from what was asked without being flagged
findings.principle: If the delivered artifact differs in shape from what was asked, a different format, a subset, an extra, or a substitution forced by the environment, the difference is named in the first three lines with the reason. Never leave it for the owner to notice.
findings.why: A silent shape change is the failure mode the estate already names as most expensive (rule 10, silent detour), but rule 10 governs the ACT of detouring. Nothing governs the REPORT of a delivery that came out a different shape for legitimate reasons.
findings.local_evidence: This run: global rule 0.5 requires a cloudflare tunnel link for any visual delivery. cloudflared's own pre-check shows UDP and TCP 7844 blocked to both edge regions in this environment, so no tunnel can exist. The delivery shape had to change, and under current rules nothing requires me to say so up front.
findings.absence_proof: grep -ri 'shape|substitut|different format|deliverable differs' ~/.claude/REPORT_SYSTEM.md CLAUDE.md returns rule 10's silent-detour ban, which is about the decision, not the disclosure.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: rule 10 bans the silent detour. It assumes the detour was a choice; an environment-forced shape change is not a choice and falls outside it.
